    East-West Pipeline continued to provide export flexibility, with additional overseas storage and new export routes being explored
    Acquisition of 49% stake in HUMAIN, involving a transfer of assets and approximately $2.6 billion in cash contributions, expands footprint in high-growth AI sector
    Shareholders’ agreement signed to form mineral exploration and hard-rock mining joint venture, leveraging Upstream expertise to expand into adjacent sector
Commenting on the results, Aramco President & CEO Amin H. Nasser said:
“Geopolitical uncertainty and attacks on key energy facilities continued to amplify the global energy supply crisis in the third quarter of 2026, with serious implications for global energy security. Despite challenges, the unwavering dedication of our workforce, our operational excellence, the flexibility of our system, and the strength of a supply network built over decades enabled us to continue delivering reliably to our customers through this extraordinary period.
“We continue to explore additional overseas storage capacity and alternative export routes to further strengthen our global supply network, and our robust operational and financial performance during this volatile period demonstrates the value of our resilience.
“Backed by our strong balance sheet, we remain focused on the disciplined execution of priority projects and on leveraging advanced technologies to enhance performance and unlock new opportunities. This is how we will continue to meet the world’s evolving energy needs and deliver value for our shareholders and customers.”
For more information, please see the 2026 Third Quarter and Nine Months Interim Report.Media contact information

October 22, 2026P&G Announces Fiscal Year 2027 First Quarter Results
Net Sales +4.0%; Organic Sales +4.0%
Diluted EPS $1.97, +1%; Core EPS $2.00, +1%
UPDATES NET SALES GUIDANCE FOR THORNE ACQUISITION
MAINTAINS FISCAL YEAR ORGANIC SALES, EPS GROWTH AND CASH RETURN GUIDANCECINCINNATI--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE:PG) reported first quarter fiscal year 2027 net sales of $23.3 billion, an increase of four percent versus the prior year. Organic sales, which excludes the impacts of foreign exchange and acquisitions and divestitures, also increased four percent versus the prior year. Diluted net earnings per share were $1.97, an increase of one percent versus prior year as the increase in net sales was partially offset by an increase in operating costs. Core earnings per share were $2.00, an increase of one percent versus the prior year.
Operating cash flow was $5.8 billion, and net earnings were $4.8 billion for the quarter. Free cash flow productivity was 93%. Free cash flow productivity is calculated as operating cash flow less capital spending, as a percentage of net earnings. The Company returned $3.9 billion of cash to shareowners via $2.6 billion of dividend payments and $1.3 billion of share repurchases.

We remain committed to our strategy to delight consumers with superior products at a superior value by putting the consumer first in everything we do. We are confident in the near term and excited about the future.”
July - September Quarter Discussion

Pricing had a minor positive impact on sales for the quarter.

Beauty segment organic sales increased five percent versus year ago. Hair Care organic sales increased mid-single digits driven by innovation-based pricing in North America and Latin America, favorable product mix and an increase in unit volume. Personal Care organic sales increased mid-single digits driven by volume growth in Greater China and Europe and favorable product mix, partially offset by trade investments. Skin Care organic sales increased mid-single digits due to favorable premium product mix and a unit volume increase in North America.
Grooming segment organic sales increased five percent versus year ago driven by innovation-based pricing, primarily in North America and IMETA, and favorable product mix.
Health Care segment organic sales increased three percent versus year ago. Oral Care organic sales increased low single digits driven by premium product mix and innovation-based pricing, partially offset by a unit volume decline. Personal Health Care organic sales increased low single digits due to higher pricing, primarily in North America and Latin America, and favorable product mix, partially offset by a unit volume decline.
Fabric and Home Care segment organic sales increased five percent versus year ago. Fabric Care organic sales increased mid-single digits driven by volume increases in North America and Europe and favorable geographic mix. Home Care organic sales also increased mid-single digits driven by volume increases in North America and Europe and favorable product mix.
Baby, Feminine and Family Care segment organic sales increased three percent versus year ago. Baby Care organic sales increased mid-single digits driven by a unit volume increase, primarily in Greater China and North America, and favorable premium product mix, partially offset by lower pricing, primarily in North America. Feminine Care organic sales increased low single digits driven by favorable product mix and innovation-based pricing, primarily in North America, partially offset by a unit volume decline in Europe. Family Care organic sales increased low single digits driven by a unit volume increase, partially offset by merchandising investments.
Diluted net earnings per share increased by one percent to $1.97. Core earnings per share increased one percent to $2.00 and Currency-neutral Core EPS was unchanged versus the prior year.
Reported gross margin for the quarter decreased 160 basis points versus the prior year. Core gross margin and currency-neutral Core gross margin for the quarter decreased 150 basis points versus the prior year and excluded the impact from incremental restructuring charges. The decrease was driven by 140 basis points of higher costs from commodities, 140 basis points of product reinvestments, 50 basis points of unfavorable mix and 10 basis points of rounding and other items, partially offset by 120 basis points of gross productivity savings, 50 basis points of tariff impact from lower costs and recognized recoveries and 20 basis points of increased pricing.
Reported selling, general and administrative expense (SG&A) as a percentage of sales declined 90 basis points versus year ago. Core SG&A as a percentage of sales decreased 80 basis points versus year ago and decreased 70 basis points on a currency-neutral basis. Core SG&A excluded the impact from incremental restructuring charges. The decline was driven by 130 basis points of productivity savings and 100 basis points of net sales growth leverage, partially offset by 120 basis points of reinvestments and 40 basis points of rounding and other items.
Reported operating margin for the quarter decreased 70 basis points versus the prior year. Excluding the impact of non-core restructuring charges, core operating margin decreased 80 basis points versus the prior year and decreased 90 basis points on a currency-neutral basis. Core operating margin included gross productivity savings of 250 basis points.
Fiscal Year 2027 Guidance
P&G updated its guidance range for fiscal 2027 all-in sales growth to be in the range of two to four percent versus the prior year, reflecting the acquisition of Thorne as of October 1, 2026. The Company maintained its outlook for organic sales growth in the range of one to three percent versus the prior year. Included in the organic sales growth guidance is a headwind of 30 to 50 basis points from brand, product form and go-to-market discontinuations.
P&G maintained its fiscal 2027 diluted net earnings per share growth to be in the range of one to five percent versus fiscal 2026 diluted net EPS of $6.62. P&G also maintained its fiscal 2027 core earnings per share growth to be in the range of in-line to three percent versus fiscal 2026 core EPS of $6.89. This outlook equates to a range of $6.89 to $7.11 per share, with a mid-point estimate of $7.00, or an increase of approximately one and a half percent.
P&G now expects a commodity cost headwind of approximately $1.4 billion after tax driven by higher raw materials, energy and transportation costs, $300 million after-tax from higher net interest expense, $150 million after-tax from lower non-operating income and $50 million after-tax from unfavorable foreign exchange rates. Combined, these impacts equate to a headwind of $0.79 per share for fiscal 2027, or an eleven percent drag on core EPS growth.
The Company is not able to reconcile its forward-looking non-GAAP cash flow and tax rate measures without unreasonable efforts given the unpredictability of the timing and amounts of discrete items, such as acquisitions, divestitures, or impairments, which could significantly impact GAAP results.
P&G now expects a core effective tax rate to be in the range of 20% to 21% in fiscal 2027.
Capital spending is estimated to be in the range of four and a half to five and a half percent of fiscal 2027 net sales.
P&G continues to expect free cash flow productivity of 85% to 90% and expects to pay over $10 billion in dividends and to repurchase approximately $5 billion of common shares in fiscal 2027.

documents.title: Head & Shoulders Launches All-New Scalp Care Collection to Prove Healthier Hair Starts at the Scalp

October 15, 2026Head & Shoulders Launches All-New Scalp Care Collection to Prove Healthier Hair Starts at the Scalp
A skincare-powered innovation for clinically proven scalp care from the #1 US Dermatologist recommended anti-dandruff brandCINCINNATI--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Head & Shoulders today unveiled its new Scalp Care Collection, a line of skincare-inspired shampoos, conditioners and treatments built to care for the scalp while delivering the hair benefits people desire most. The collection features three personalized regimens designed for specific scalp needs that are clinically proven to remove visible flakes at the source and repair the scalp barrier for healthier-looking hair, bringing a new level of beauty to a brand best known for scalp care.
“This launch marks a bold new chapter for the brand, one that removes dandruff and moves beyond just managing flakes to transforming how hair looks and feels by taking a skincare-inspired approach to common scalp concerns,” said Matt Krehbiel, Vice President, Head & Shoulders. “We're showing people that exceptional hair starts at the scalp through educational content and partnerships with trusted experts and relatable voices in beauty.”
The collection targets the root causes of scalp damage in three ways: gently removing flakes, fighting oxidative scalp stress and restoring the scalp barrier. The formulas feature the brand's HydraSC+ Complex, built on either 1.8% salicylic acid, which exfoliates and lifts away flakes and buildup, or 1% zinc pyrithione, which targets Malassezia, the scalp microbe associated with dandruff. Consumers can select the regimen best suited to their scalp concerns:
Scalp Soothe with Niacinamide (for itchy* scalps): Instant cooling and dandruff itch relief from the first use, with shampoo delivering an added boost of hair shine. The regimen includes the Cooling Shampoo and Cooling Scalp Spray, which can be used up to 4 times daily for relief between washes.
Scalp Purify with Salicylic Acid (for oily scalps): Instantly removes up to 99% of flakes, oil and buildup for up to 5x more volume in one color-safe, non-stripping routine. The regimen includes the Clarifying Pre-Shampoo and Volumizing Shampoo.
Scalp Restore with Bio-Ceramides (for dry scalps): Delivers 72-moisture lock and restores the scalp barrier for hydrated hair. The sulfate-free regimen includes the Nourishing Shampoo, Nourishing Conditioner and Nourishing Leave-On Serum.
Shampoos and conditioners within the Head & Shoulders Scalp Care Collection are now available at Walmart with a suggested MSRP of $11.99. Treatments and expanded availability at Walmart and other retailers arrive this November. For more information, visit headandshoulders.com or follow Head & Shoulders on Instagram, TikTok and Facebook.

October 14, 2026Think Your Toilet Paper Is Good Enough? Charmin Thinks You and Your Butt Deserve Better.
Porsha Williams partners with Charmin to encourage consumers to raise their standards with Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, the brand's biggest innovation in more than a decade.
Charmin introduces new Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, the brand's biggest Ultra Strong innovation in more than a decade.
Distinguished by its 3D durable weave texture, the new Charmin Ultra Strong now has wider sheets that clean better so you can use up to 50% less*.
Porsha Williams is teaming up with Charmin to help raise toilet paper standards, bringing the brand's wider-sheet innovation to life through social content and an immersive New York City experience where consumers can discover the difference for themselves.
CINCINNATI--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Today, Charmin unveils the new Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, the brand's biggest Ultra Strong innovation in more than a decade. Designed to deliver a better clean, new Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets replaces the existing Ultra Strong product line with a wider-sheet design that provides more coverage and helps consumers use up to 50% less* toilet paper. Built on the belief that better changes everything, the innovation is designed to challenge what consumers expect from their toilet paper by delivering an upgrade consumers didn’t know they needed.
For many shoppers, toilet paper has long been a category where people settle for what's familiar, but Charmin wants to challenge that notion. Featuring its signature 3D diamond weave texture, Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets aims to raise the bar for what consumers should expect from their toilet paper. By combining greater coverage with the strength and durability people already love, the innovation creates an upgraded experience that redefines what “good enough” should look and feel like in the bathroom. That’s what happens when you get the upgrade you didn’t know you needed - better changes everything.
"Consumers may not think to ask for a wider sheet, but they do know a better clean when they feel it. With Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, we've taken something people use every day and made it meaningfully better by delivering more coverage, a better clean, and helping consumers use less,” said Alex Perez, Charmin Brand Vice President, Procter & Gamble. “For years, Ultra Strong has provided consumers strength and durability. Now, Charmin is building on that legacy with an innovation designed to redefine what consumers should expect from their toilet paper. Charmin Ultra Strong truly delivers a differentiated clean that consumers can’t unfeel.”
To help raise these toilet paper standards, Charmin is partnering with media personality, entrepreneur and Charmin loyalist Porsha Williams. She will be involved in the brand’s social campaign and will serve as the host of Charmin’s Wider Sheet immersive NYC experience on October 20. Visitors can join in on the fun by snapping photos with a one-of-a-kind Charmin vehicle inspired by the brand's campaign, meet the beloved Charmin bears and get up close with the new Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets to see the difference for themselves.
“Listen, I’m not someone who settles for basic, so why would I do it with my toilet paper?” said Porsha Williams. “When I tried Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets, I was mad nobody told me sooner. More coverage, a better clean, AND using less? That’s the kind of upgrade I can get behind. And honestly? Your backside will thank you."
New Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets is available now at major retailers nationwide and online. To learn more, visit Charmin.com and follow @Charmin on social media.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets?
Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets is the newest innovation in the Charmin Ultra Strong portfolio and the brand's biggest Ultra Strong innovation in more than a decade. The new Charmin Ultra Strong now features wider sheets that clean better.
How does the wider-sheet design improve the cleaning experience?
The New Charmin Ultra Strong has wider sheets* that cleans better* with more durable weave texture per sheet*, and sheets that are 4X stronger so you can use 50% less
How does Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets help consumers use less toilet paper?
Charmin Ultra Strong now features wider sheets* that clean better, so consumers can use up to 50% less* toilet paper.
What makes Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets different from previous versions?
The introduction of Wider Sheets marks the first major innovation to Charmin Ultra Strong in more than a decade. The enhanced design builds on the product’s signature strength while introducing increased coverage that helps improve the overall cleaning experience.
Where can consumers purchase Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets?
Charmin Ultra Strong with Wider Sheets is available at major retailers nationwide and online. Consumers can visit Charmin.com for additional product information and retailer availability.
Are Wider Sheets the new standard for Charmin Ultra Strong?
Yes, as Charmin's biggest Ultra Strong innovation in more than a decade, Wider Sheets are designed to raise expectations for what consumers should expect from their toilet paper. By providing a better clean while using less, Wider Sheets challenge the idea that "good enough" is good enough and help establish a new standard for toilet paper.
*vs. leading 1 ply USA bargain brand

“With geopolitical uncertainty and declining global inventories, the importance of both energy security and energy addition has never been clearer. “We have entered the second half of the year with solid financial and operating momentum with one of the strongest balance sheets in the sector, sustainable and progressive base dividend distributions, and a clear focus on our strategic growth objectives. Even through periods of uncertainty, Aramco has stayed anchored to its long-term priorities. (“Tesla”) entered into the following credit agreements:•$20.0 billion senior unsecured three-year delayed draw term loan facility (the “Term Loan Facility”) pursuant to a Delayed Draw Term Loan Credit Agreement, dated as of September 29, 2026 (the “DDTL Credit Agreement”), by and among Tesla, as borrower, Citibank, N.A. (“Citi”), as administrative agent, and the lenders and other agents party thereto.•$8.0 billion senior unsecured five-year revolving facility (the “Five-Year Revolving Facility”) pursuant to a Five-Year Revolving Credit Agreement, dated as of September 29, 2026 (the “Five-Year Revolving Credit Agreement”), by and among Tesla, as borrower, Wells Fargo Bank, National Association (“WF Bank”), as administrative agent, and the lenders, issuing banks and other agents party thereto.•$2.0 billion senior unsecured 364-day revolving credit facility (the “364-Day Revolving Facility”) pursuant to a 364-Day Revolving Credit Agreement, dated as of September 29, 2026 (the “364-Day Revolving Credit Agreement”), by and among Tesla, as borrower, WF Bank, as administrative agent, and the lenders and other agents party thereto.The 364-Day Revolving Facility, together with the Five-Year Revolving Facility, are referred to herein as the “Revolving Facilities”, and the Revolving Facilities, together with the Term Loan Facility, are referred to herein as the “Facilities”. The 364-Day Revolving Credit Agreement, together with the Five-Year Revolving Credit Agreement, are referred to herein as the “Revolving Credit Agreements”, and the Revolving Credit Agreements, together with the DDTL Credit Agreement, are referred to herein as the “Credit Agreements”.Delayed Draw Term Loan FacilityTesla may draw upon the Term Loan Facility from time to time and no more than ten times during the 18-month period following the closing date. The undrawn commitments under the Term Loan Facility will be automatically reduced to $10.0 billion on the first anniversary of the closing date and to $5.0 billion 15 months after the closing date, and any remaining undrawn commitments will terminate 18 months after the closing date. Loans outstanding under the Term Loan Facility will mature on September 29, 2029.Five-Year Revolving Credit FacilityTesla may draw upon the Five-Year Revolving Facility from time to time. Loans under the Five-Year Revolving Facility may be denominated in U.S. dollars, pounds sterling or euros. The Five-Year Revolving Facility provides for the issuance of letters of credit in an aggregate amount of up to $500 million.The Five-Year Revolving Facility terminates, and all outstanding loans and other amounts thereunder, if any, will become due and payable on September 29, 2031. Tesla may request up to two one-year extensions of the Five-Year Revolving Facility, subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions.364-Day Revolving Credit FacilityTesla may draw upon the 364-Day Revolving Facility from time to time. Loans under the 364-Day Revolving Facility are denominated in U.S. dollars.The 364-Day Revolving Facility terminates, and all outstanding loans and other amounts thereunder, if any, will become due and payable on September 28, 2027. Subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions, Tesla may exercise a term-out option to extend the maturity of all or a ratable portion of the loans outstanding on that date for an additional year. Tesla may increase the total commitments under the Revolving Credit Agreements by up to an additional $4.0 billion across the Revolving Facilities, subject to certain conditions, potentially increasing the Revolving Facilities to $14.0 billion in the aggregate.Use of Proceeds and PricingThe proceeds of loans under the Facilities, and letters of credit issued under the Five-Year Revolving Facility, may be used for general corporate purposes or for any other purpose not otherwise prohibited by the applicable Credit Agreement. No loans were outstanding under the Facilities as of September 29, 2026.U.S. dollar-denominated borrowings under the Facilities accrue interest, at Tesla’s election, at a variable rate based on either Term SOFR or an alternate base rate, in each case plus an applicable margin. Borrowings denominated in pounds sterling under the Five-Year Revolving Facility will accrue interest at a rate based on SONIA, and borrowings denominated in euros under the Five-Year Revolving Facility will accrue interest at a rate based on adjusted EURIBOR, in each case plus an applicable margin. 	To our Shareholders:
General Motors delivered another solid quarter of earnings, driven by the appeal of our product portfolio, the agility of our team, and disciplined execution.
Our employees, our dealers and our suppliers are all making important contributions that continue to drive our success. Their commitment enables us to win in a dynamic market, and their efforts are leading us to raise our 2026 guidance for the second time.
The business continues to perform very well. Customer demand in North America remains strong driven by our very attractive lineup of pickups and SUVs. Pricing is consistent, and we delivered the best quarter and first half ever for new Super Cruise-equipped vehicles.
Our 8.6% EBIT-adjusted margin in North America was up 2.5 points from a year ago, and we continue to lower our warranty costs, reduce EV losses, and increase operating efficiency. In addition, GM International, inclusive of our China joint ventures, was profitable.
We expect these trends will continue to strengthen our performance into 2027 and beyond because we have multiple engines of margin expansion and growth while maintaining our capital discipline.
Our vehicle portfolio continues to get stronger, with the launch of the next-generation Chevrolet Silverado LD and GMC Sierra LD starting in December
Our software and services ecosystem is expanding
Our manufacturing and sourcing footprint is becoming more efficient, and we will be onshoring significant production to further reduce our tariff exposure
And growth businesses like GM Defense and GM Insurance are creating additional avenues for value creation
All of this supports our commitment to ongoing margin expansion. We know there’s more work ahead, but we are building from a position of strength with a proven track record of execution, and I’d like to thank you for your continued confidence in the General Motors team.
Mary Barra

GM Q1 2026 letter to shareholders
		2026-04-28
        		News and events
				,
        		Financial
				,

	To our Shareholders,
In the first quarter of 2026, General Motors once again delivered strong financial performance , driven by our strategic product portfolio and disciplined execution by our teams, dealers, and suppliers.
Our EBIT-adjusted of $4.3 billion surpassed our expectations even after excluding a $ 500 million tariff adjustment following a recent U.S. Supreme Court decision. To reflect the flow-through of this adjustment, we are raising our full-year EBIT-adjusted guidance by $500 million, to a range of $13.5 billion to $15.5 billion.
We have solid momentum in our core operations: We maintained overall sales leadership in the U.S. and Canada. We led the U.S. industry in full -size pickup sales and share, with 42% of the market, and we were #1 in Fleet, including Commercial deliveries. In addition, we were #2 in EVs with growing market share, and #1 in Ca nada .
I would also like to highlight our crossovers because they complement our full-size truck leadership. Since we began refreshing our lineup in 2023 , crossovers have grown from just over 40% of GM sales to more than 46%, and no one offers more budget-friendly choices. At the same time, crossovers like the Chevrolet Trax and Equinox, the Buick Envista and GMC Terrain, and the Chevrolet Traverse and GMC Acadia, have become significant contributors to our profitability.
Complementing our performance in North America was our 6th consecutive profitable quarter in China, and higher year-over-year results in GMI, excluding China.
Looking forward, we remain focused on delivering 8–10% North America margins this year, OnStar, including Super Cruise, is contributing to high-margin revenue growth, and we are advancing automated driving technology in ways that differentiate GM.
We are clearly operating in a very dynamic environment, which isn’t unusual for this industry. That’s why we have had a multi-year focus to ensure we have the right products, the right team, and a strong balance sheet supported by healthy cash flows to achieve our long-term goals and consistently execute our capital allocation strategy.
As we move forward, I’m confident this will continue to differentiate GM and support long-term value creation for our owners.
Thank you for your continued confidence in General Motors.

documents.title: Aramco and Maaden sign shareholders’ agreement to form joint venture to unlock new frontier for mineral exploration and hard-rock mining in Saudi Arabia
documents.raw_text:
Aramco and Maaden sign shareholders’ agreement to form joint venture to unlock new frontier for mineral exploration and hard-rock mining in Saudi ArabiaNews|DHAHRAN|August 18, 2026PartnershipsOperations
    Joint venture would combine Aramco’s subsurface knowledge, advanced AI tools, and powerful computational capabilities with Maaden’s mining and mineral exploration expertise
    Exploration activities to mainly focus on copper, alongside other energy transition minerals, in a zone equivalent to nearly 10% of Saudi Arabia’s total land area
    Joint venture aims to accelerate discovery, advancing Saudi Arabia’s role in the global energy transition value chain
Aramco, one of the world’s leading integrated energy and chemicals companies, and Maaden, one of the world’s fastest‑growing mining companies and the largest multi‑commodity mining and metals producer in the Middle East, today announced the signing of a shareholders’ agreement to form a Joint Venture (JV) to unlock new opportunities in mineral exploration and hard-rock mining in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Combining the strengths of two leaders in their respective fields, the JV would focus on copper and other minerals critical to the energy transition. Plans for the JV were first disclosed in January 2025.
The JV is expected to be owned 51% by Maaden and 49% by Aramco and would focus on exploration across Zone-4, also known as the Transition Zone, within the Arabian Platform. It represents a major new opportunity for mineral discovery in the Kingdom. Spanning approximately 182,000 square kilometers, nearly 10% of Saudi Arabia’s total land area, the expected exploration area stretches along a 100-kilometer-wide zone running parallel to the Arabian Shield.
Saleh M. Al Saleh, Aramco Vice President of Transition Minerals, said: “Over 90 years, Aramco has accumulated and analyzed the largest amount of geological and geophysical data ever acquired in a single basin for the Kingdom. This partnership intends to leverage this legacy information to find minerals in the JV area within the basin. Maaden’s expertise, our people, high-performance computing, and AI are expected to play a pivotal role in accelerating the discovery of key transition minerals at low cost.”
Darryl Clark, Maaden Executive Vice President for Exploration, said: “Maaden has been advancing one of the world’s largest single jurisdiction exploration programs across the Arabian Shield to help unlock the Kingdom’s mineral potential. This joint venture would take that ambition into a new area. By combining Maaden’s exploration and development expertise with Aramco’s extraordinary knowledge of the Arabian Platform, we would have an opportunity to move faster, explore smarter, and create new opportunities to discover the minerals that will power the energy transition.”
Copper, which is increasingly significant for electric vehicles, power networks, energy storage, and renewable energy systems, would be a main focus of the JV. Copper is a major metal making up over 20% of the $1.2 trillion mined metals market. The copper market is currently valued at approximately $250 billion and is projected to grow to over $400 billion by 2035. The JV would also explore for other energy transition minerals including zinc, lead, and rare earth elements that are expected to be crucial to industries of the future.
Leveraging advanced computational algorithms, AI, and high-performance computing, the JV intends to target areas most likely to contain copper and valuable minerals, accelerating the path from regional screening to target definition and discovery. This is expected to support long-term sector development, reinforce the Kingdom’s role in the global minerals value chain, and help meet rising demand for transition minerals.
The effectiveness of the shareholders’ agreement and the incorporation of the JV is conditional upon the fulfillment of certain condition precedents, including, but not limited to, obtaining all the required corporate and regulatory approvals and antitrust clearance.Media contact information

documents.title: Aramco enhances its global partnership ecosystem through collaboration with French companies
documents.raw_text:
Aramco enhances its global partnership ecosystem through collaboration with French companiesNews|Dhahran|August 24, 2026Partnerships
    Agreements and MoU have potential combined value of more than $3.7 billion
    Partnerships are expected to strengthen Aramco’s supply chain ecosystem, enhance operational continuity and efficiency, advance industrial artificial intelligence and digital technologies, and deliver economic value to Saudi Arabia and France
    Focus areas span project support, capacity building and capability development, technology transfer and innovation, and supply chain resilience
Aramco, one of the world’s leading integrated energy and chemicals companies, today announced agreements and a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with a potential combined value of more than $3.7 billion with French companies.
These collaborative efforts are expected to strengthen Aramco’s supply chain ecosystem, enhance operational continuity and efficiency, advance industrial artificial intelligence and digital technologies, and deliver economic value to the Kingdom and France.
Amin H. Nasser, Aramco President & CEO, attended the French-Saudi Investment Roundtable Meeting, during which the agreements and MoU signed by Aramco and Aramco Digital were announced.
The collaborations focus on project support, capacity building and capability development, technology transfer and innovation, and supply chain resilience. They include:
    Corporate procurement agreement for drilling equipment
    Purchase agreement for Oil Country Tubular Goods (OCTG)
    Memorandum of Understanding with Aramco Digital that establishes a framework for potential collaboration in industrial AI, virtual twin/digital twin technologies, and related technologies, including potential applications in the oil and gas sector
Media contact information
All media enquiries are handled by Aramco’s Media Communications & Coordination Department, Dhahran, Saudi Arabia.
